clue.text: Homespun, such clothing is hardly one's Sunday best

definitions.text: such clothing is hardly one's Sunday best
definitions.meaning: clothes for ordinary weekdays, not the smart outfit kept for church

explanation.surface: A remark that plain homemade garments are not what one wears to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and plain is a synonym of homespun, and weekday clothes are the opposite of Sunday best.

clue.text: Duty deferred Fleming's fortune here?

definitions.meaning: goods held in a bonded warehouse have their customs duty postponed until release
Ian Fleming made his money from his James Bond novels

explanation.surface: A tax postponed, and a question about where a novelist's wealth lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonded goods await payment of duty, and Ian Fleming's riches came from his Bond books.

clue.text: Liberal old hunt gathering circles great house

indicators.note: the pieces are gathered up and jumbled together into a new order

parts.note: two circles are two round O shapes

explanation.surface: A Liberal joins an old-fashioned fox hunt as it rides in circles round a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' is the anagram signal, drawing the pieces together into a new order. LUTON HOO is a stately home in Bedfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton Hoo is an English country mansion, an example of a great house.

clue.text: What's on in Aqua Sulis is inspired

definitions.text: What's on in Aqua Sulis is inspired

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the clue says something is in the city

parts.note: Aquae Sulis was the Roman name for the English spa city of Bath

explanation.surface: A question about what's showing at the Roman baths, answered as something inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: what you breathe in is inspired. Bath is the spa city in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Air drawn into the lungs is inhaled, or inspired, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: See 12
Some way into a female utopia

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
AVE is short for avenue, a kind of way

explanation.surface: A path leading into a woman's perfect world.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopia is an ideal place, as paradise is.

clue.text: He shortened the lives of his subjects

definitions.text: He shortened the lives of his subjects

parts.words: He shortened the lives of his subjects
parts.note: sounds like an executioner, but refers to a 17th-century writer of brief biographies, published as Brief Lives

explanation.surface: A sinister ruler who cut his subjects' lives short.
explanation.definitionFit: John Aubrey wrote Brief Lives, short biographies, so he literally made lives brief.

clue.text: More than one thus addressed in Lehrer's "____ and shet-ma-mouth land"

definitions.meaning: the Southern US plural form of address for several people
Tom Lehrer's satirical song about the American South calls it the land of this phrase and shut-my-mouth

explanation.surface: A lyric from a Tom Lehrer song about the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: In Southern American speech this phrase is the plural of you, used to address a group.

clue.text: Its advantage, first off, could be most effective

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to form something else
the first letter of the word is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that the first-mover advantage could be the strongest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops the A from advantage, leaving DVANTAGE; with ITS, 'could be' rearranges ITSDVANTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastating means overwhelmingly effective, as in a devastating argument.

clue.text: Musical party with style

parts.note: Hair is a famous 1960s rock musical
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A stage show and a celebration done with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is a hairstyle, the way one's hair is arranged.

clue.text: The Roman city of Morecambe, accepting you, say, but not me, sadly

indicators.note: the shortened town name takes in another letter, as a host accepts a guest
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are muddled
the letters of me are excluded from the word

parts.note: the letter U is said like the word you

explanation.surface: A sad tale of the Lancashire seaside town taking in a newcomer but not the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes M and E from MORECAMBE, leaving ORECAB; 'accepting' adds U, and 'sadly' rearranges ORECABU. Morecambe is a seaside resort in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eboracum was the Roman name for York, so it is a Roman city.

clue.text: Cut Nigel Dempster's contribution

indicators.note: a contribution is a small part, here a run of letters taken from the name

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist's piece is axed by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Dempster was a famous British gossip columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: To geld is to castrate, i.e. to cut an animal.

clue.text: "And ______" (13) Aha! The mind lives on. Hold on! A resurrection!

indicators.note: the words are raised up again in a new form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of triumph that the mind survives death and rises again.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to a poem by the poet at 13-across, whose title opens with And.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dylan Thomas poem And Death Shall Have No Dominion is named by its opening word and author.

clue.text: Holy man with DTs a shaky poet

indicators.note: shaky letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A saint suffering from the trembling of alcohol withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: DTs are delirium tremens, the shakes of a heavy drinker, a nod to the poet's drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas was a celebrated Welsh poet.

clue.text: A sailor, I? O, I can climb from from the word go!

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, an ordinary sailor

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

explanation.surface: A sailor's excited cry that he can climb the rigging from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' reverses OITIN to NITIO. The first 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ab initio is Latin for from the beginning, i.e. from the word go.

clue.text: The magpies left after Tay disaster: extraordinary!

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the first one
a disaster throws things into disorder

parts.note: Pica is the genus name of magpies

explanation.surface: Magpies fleeing after a calamity on the Scottish river Tay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges TAY as ATY. The Tay is Scotland's longest river, known for the Tay Bridge disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Here dragons floor the war department band

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, the UK war department
a band or ring is the round letter O

explanation.surface: Mythical beasts knock down the military band.
explanation.definitionFit: Komodo is the Indonesian island famous as home of the Komodo dragon.

clue.text: Franklin, a noted 18?

parts.note: the surname of a famed soul singer, with 18 pointing to the clue for a soul sister, so we want her first name

explanation.surface: A query about a celebrated Franklin's genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin, the Queen of Soul, was a famous soul sister.

clue.text: Sam and Dave hit their only sibling, say?

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the words sound

parts.note: one's only sister would be a sole sister

explanation.surface: A soul duo's single dedicated to their one sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam and Dave were a 1960s US soul duo; Soul Sister, Brown Sugar was one of their hits.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul Sister, Brown Sugar was a 1968 hit single for the duo Sam and Dave.

clue.text: Refined oil to soak up? Hang about!

indicators.note: refined oil has been processed and changed, so its letters are reworked
in a down entry, up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it

explanation.surface: Instructions for treating oil, followed by an impatient call to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined' turns OIL into LOI; 'up' reverses RET into TER.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly.

clue.text: Totter under this omnium-gatherum?

definitions.meaning: a totter is a rag-and-bone man, who carries a sack of rags

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering beneath a heap of odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a confused jumble, a miscellany, and literally a bag of rags for a totter.

clue.text: Sun King's house once 10

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Richard III calls Edward IV the sun of his own dynasty, and that royal house shares the city's name
the city that was once the Roman one at 10-across

explanation.surface: A royal residence once linked to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward IV belonged to the House of York, and Roman Eboracum is now the city of York.

clue.text: See 12
Conviviality of the Gordons' theatre

definitions.meaning: a playhouse name meaning merriment, used for theatres in several British and Irish cities

explanation.surface: The merry spirit of a family's playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is cheerful festivity, a synonym of conviviality, and also a common theatre name.

clue.text: Evidently abstemious Pushkin hero

definitions.meaning: someone who has had just a single measure of the juniper spirit seems to drink little
the title character of Pushkin's verse novel, a bored Russian dandy named Eugene

explanation.surface: A Russian literary hero who drinks moderately.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Onegin is Pushkin's hero, and split as one gin it describes a moderate drinker.

clue.text: "Yes, we 5 across ____s"

parts.note: a popular 1920s novelty song title with its fruit missing, completed by the words at 5-across

explanation.surface: A line from an old music-hall song about a fruit shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: The song is Yes, We Have No Bananas, so the gap takes the fruit's name.
